# tar test fixtures

Generated by a one-off python3 tarfile invocation (the oracle;
python3 3.14). No generator script is committed: the recipe is
python3's tarfile module writing each archive below with explicit
modes, mtimes, uid/gid 0, and empty uname/gname, then re-reading
every fixture through `tarfile.getmembers()` to derive
`manifest.edn` (the realism check: the manifest IS the oracle's own
read, so the fixture bytes were parseable by the reference reader
before any mino reader existed).

Golden (benign) archives:

- `basic.tar` -- ustar: a regular file with an explicit mode and
  mtime, a zero-mtime file (the nil-mtime pin), a directory, a
  nested file, a symlink entry, and a hardlink entry pointing at an
  earlier member.
- `longname.tar` -- pax: one member whose 124-char basename cannot
  fit the ustar name field, so the name travels in a pax `path`
  record; the listing must surface the full logical name and never
  the PaxHeader pseudo-entry.

Hostile archives (structurally valid tar; the names, linknames, or
size fields are the attack, so extract hardening is what rejects
them, never a parse failure):

- `traversal.tar` -- member named `../escaped.txt`.
- `absolute.tar` -- member with an absolute name.
- `linktarget.tar` -- symlink entry whose linkname escapes the
  extraction root (`../../mino-tar-link-evil`).
- `linkwrite.tar` -- symlink `sub -> ..` followed by
  `sub/evil.txt`: writing the second member through the
  materialized link would land outside the extraction root.
- `hardlink.tar` -- hardlink entry whose linkname escapes the
  extraction root.
- `sizebomb.tar` -- valid ustar header declaring ~8 GiB (octal
  size field at its maximum) with no payload; the declared size
  runs past EOF.
- `size256.tar` -- GNU base-256 size field carrying int64 max; the
  512-block round-up overflows a signed 64-bit offset.

`manifest.edn` pins the archive SHA-256s, the oracle-read entry
vectors (name, size, mode, mtime, type, linkname) in archive order,
and the SHA-256 of every regular member's bytes. The size-field
fixtures carry only the archive sha: python parses their headers
(asserted at generation) but cannot list past the declared sizes.
